A Farmer's Delight cooking pot that pulls its ingredients from your storage system. It still needs a heat source beneath it to cook.

Bind it with sneak + right-click on any block of your system. A Resonating Beacon has to be in range for the pot to connect. Pick a recipe from the panel and the pot pulls everything it needs, from your inventory first and then the system.
Meals stay in the pot until you give it serving containers, by hand or with the request button. Like the rest of your system, it needs no power.
book.refineddelight.guide.landing: Farmer's Delight cooking, wired into your Magitech storage system. $(br2)Everything the regular cooking pot does, plus ingredients on tap from storage.
category.refineddelight.main.description: The Resonating Cooking Pot: binding, cooking and serving.
entry.refineddelight.wireless_cooking_po: The $(item)Resonating Cooking Pot$() is a Farmer's Delight cooking pot that can reach into your storage system for its ingredients.$(br2)It is still a cooking pot: it needs a $(thing)heat source$() beneath it, and it cooks the same recipes at the same speed.
Crafted from a Cooking Pot, Illuminite, Ender Pearls and a Divine Runic Processor.

Hold the pot and $(thing)sneak + right-click$() any block of your system, like a cable or a Glyphic Repository. That only tells the pot $(o)which system$() to use, so pick something that will stay put.$(br2)You must sneak: a plain right-click opens that block's own screen instead.$(br2)To actually connect, your system needs a $(thing)Resonating Beacon$() whose range covers the pot. Fit the Beacon with $(thing)Range Upgrades$() and the pot reaches exactly as far as your Resonating Console does.

Load ingredients by hand and it behaves exactly like the regular pot.$(br2)Or open the $(thing)recipe panel$() and click a recipe: the pot pulls a single serving. $(thing)Shift-click$() pulls as many as it can hold at once.$(br2)Ingredients come from $(o)your inventory first$(), then the system.

Cooked meals collect inside the pot, up to $(thing)64$() no matter how small the meal's own stack size.$(br2)They only come out when the recipe's $(thing)serving container$() is provided: place bowls or bottles in the container slot, or press the $(thing)request$() button to pull them from the system.$(br2)Break the pot and any waiting meal travels inside it.

Just like the rest of your system, the pot needs $(o)no power at all$(). The battery gauge on its screen is only for show and always reads full.$(br2)The binding and any waiting meal both survive breaking and replacing the pot.
